name: Calcium gluconate
executiveSummary: IV calcium salt. Adult hyperK / symptomatic hypocalcemia: **1–2 g (10–20 mL of 10%)** slow IV. Pediatrics: **0.5–1 mL/kg** of 10% gluconate (usual max **10–20 mL**/dose). Monitor ECG; necrosis risk if extravasation.
indications:
## Indications

- Hyperkalemia with ECG changes (membrane stabilization).
- Symptomatic hypocalcemia; calcium-channel blocker toxicity / hypermagnesemia (protocols).

## Precautions

- **Do not mix with bicarbonate or phosphate** (precipitates). Prefer central line or reliable peripheral IV.
- Stop if bradycardia. Address concurrent hypokalemia thoughtfully.
- Calcium chloride has more elemental Ca/mL — do not swap mL for mL.

> 10% ampoule: ~**100 mg gluconate/mL** ≈ **9 mg elemental Ca/mL** (~0.46 mEq/mL).

adulto.dose: HyperK / emergency: **10–20 mL (1–2 g)** IV over **2–5–10 min**; repeat in 5–10 min if ECG changes persist. Hypocalcemia: **1–2 g** then infusion by ionized Ca.
adulto.administration: Slow IV under monitoring; dilute if infusion (up to ~50 mg/mL). Orient. push rate **0.5–1 mL/min**.
adulto.notes: Extravasation → necrosis. Compatible with NS/D5W; not with HCO3−/PO4.

pediatrico.dose: Symptomatic hypocalcemia / hyperK: **0.5–1 mL/kg** of 10% (**50–100 mg/kg** gluconate; usual max **10 mL**/dose) over 5–10 min; may repeat or continue **~5 mL/kg/day** infusion. Asymptomatic (if no PO): **2–5 mL/kg/day**.

neonatal.dose: **1–2 mL/kg** of 10% gluconate slow IV (or per neonatal hypocalcemia protocol).

stability:
## Stability

- Prefer dedicated line; discard opened ampoule per card.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Bradycardia, hypotension if rapid; calcification/necrosis from extravasation; hypercalcemia.
